children: Arm's Chief Executive Rene Haas said he is committed to leading the company over the long-term, signing a new agreement that extends his contract through 2033.

Haas had been seen as a potential candidate to take on the top job at Nvidia after Jensen Huang resigned this month amid revelations of his extramarital affairs, including one with a suspected Chinese spy and another with an employee.

Nvidia hired executive search firm Heidrick & Struggles to lead the hunt for its next CEO, and the firm was in talks with potential candidates including Haas, The Wall Street Journal previously reported.
Haas said he's never been more confident about Arm's future.

"I believe deeply in our people, our strategy and the opportunity ahead. I'm incredibly proud of what we're building and wholly committed to realizing Arm's full potential for many years to come," Haas said in a statement.
Arm also said Haas would assume the role of vice chairman of SoftBank Group, effective Dec. 1.
